journey.title: Open the filters drawer and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: When the drawer dialog is opened via showModal(), no initial focus is set, causing focus to remain on the triggering button or the document body instead of moving inside the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Add the autofocus attribute to the close button inside the drawer so that the browser automatically focuses it when the dialog is shown, satisfying the expectation that focus enters the dialog upon opening.

edits.after: <button type="button" class="btn-close" id="filters-close" data-bs-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close" autofocus></button>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening the filters drawer, focus will move to the close button, allowing keyboard users to navigate the dialog without a pointer.
functional_risks: If the dialog is opened via a script call that expects focus elsewhere, the autofocus may shift focus unintentionally.
Duplicate autofocus elements could cause focus conflicts, but only one autofocus element exists.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, the close button (#filters-close) must receive focus.
Pressing Tab from the close button should move focus to the 'In stock' checkbox.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.

plan.root_cause: When the drawer dialog is opened via showModal(), the browser focuses the dialog element itself, not the close button. The close button has an autofocus attribute, but the native <dialog> element does not honor autofocus when shown via showModal(). The DialogBase component does not implement autofocus handling for dialogs.
plan.repair_strategy: Add autofocus attribute to the close button in the HTML, and modify DialogBase._showElement to focus the first element with autofocus after showing the dialog. This ensures keyboard focus moves into the drawer upon opening.

edits.after: <button type="button" class="btn-close" id="filters-close" data-bs-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close" autofocus></button>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening the filters drawer via keyboard (Enter on the Filters button), focus will immediately move to the close button, allowing keyboard users to navigate the dialog without a pointer. Subsequent Tab presses will move focus to the checkboxes and apply button.
functional_risks: If a dialog has multiple autofocus elements, the first one in tree order will receive focus, which may not be the intended target.
If a dialog is opened via a script call that expects focus to remain on the trigger, the autofocus will shift focus. However, this is standard dialog behavior.
The change affects all dialogs and drawers using DialogBase, but autofocus is opt-in via the attribute.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, the close button (#filters-close) must receive focus.
Pressing Tab from the close button should move focus to the 'In stock' checkbox.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.
The applied filter text should update to 'in' after pressing Enter on the Apply button.
